title: Indian Market News Brief — 19 Nov 2026 — Nifty 50
quick_read: Record foreign investor buying of over 1 lakh crore rupees in November may support Indian shares. However, US Federal Reserve signals of possible interest rate increases and a stronger US dollar could hurt market mood. How rising domestic bond yields balance against strong bank earnings remains unclear.

stories.headline: FPI stock-buying tops ₹1 trillion in November, highest-ever monthly inflow
stories.summary: Foreign portfolio investors pumped over 1 lakh crore rupees into Indian shares in November. This marks their highest-ever monthly buying in the domestic market. The buying ended a 16-month selling streak that ran from July 2025 to October 2026. Cheaper stock valuations and softer crude oil prices drove the inflows. The rising market also attracted additional foreign money.
stories.impact: May help Nifty: Huge foreign cash inflows may support large-cap benchmark shares and lift overall market sentiment.

stories.headline: Fed policymakers focused on inflation risks in October, with some seeing need for bigger rate hike
stories.summary: Federal Reserve minutes showed US policymakers focused on inflation risks during their October meeting. While interest rates were kept steady, officials discussed the need for a possible half-percentage-point rate increase. Policymakers worry that price rises are not slowing down fast enough. The US central bank faces heated debates ahead of its December meeting.
stories.impact: May hurt Nifty: Higher US interest rates can pull foreign funds away from emerging markets like India and pressure domestic shares.

stories.headline: PSBs' net profit rises 17% to Rs 1.10 lakh cr in H1 FY27; business crosses Rs 300 lakh crore
stories.summary: Public sector banks reported a 16.9 percent rise in net profit to 1.10 lakh crore rupees in the first half of the financial year. Total business surpassed 301.6 lakh crore rupees. Gross bad loans fell to 1.69 percent. The numbers reflect strong health across state-owned lenders.
stories.impact: May help Nifty: Strong profitability and cleaner balance sheets could lift state-run banking stocks.

stories.headline: India bonds reverse intraday gains to end lower as profit booking takes center stage
stories.summary: Indian government bonds gave up earlier gains as traders took profits. The 10-year benchmark bond yield rose to 7.2858 percent. Rising retail inflation has raised concerns that the Reserve Bank of India might hike rates in December. Oil price movements also guided bond market movements.
stories.impact: May hurt Nifty: Higher borrowing costs across the economy could hurt corporate profits and slow down loan growth.

stories.headline: Nvidia shares gain 3% in premarket after Q3 results, upbeat forecast top estimates: Is the AI rally back on track?
stories.summary: Nvidia shares jumped 3 percent in US premarket trading after quarterly earnings beat estimates. Revenue and profit more than doubled from a year earlier. The chipmaker gave an upbeat revenue forecast of 130 billion dollars. The strong numbers revived optimism around artificial intelligence spending.
stories.impact: May help Nifty: Strong tech earnings in the US may lift Indian software exporter stocks on better global demand hopes.

stories.headline: Goldman Sachs upgrades India to overweight, sets Nifty target of 28,500
stories.summary: Goldman Sachs raised its rating on Indian equities to overweight. The brokerage set a target of 28,500 for the Nifty index. It noted that India lagged behind other Asian markets by 83 percentage points between mid-2024 and late-2026. The firm expects Indian stocks to catch up after this underperformance.
stories.impact: May help Nifty: Positive views from global brokerages could encourage more foreign institutional buying into Indian blue-chip stocks.

stories.headline: Rupee ends flat after hitting seven-month high as firmer dollar offsets inflows
stories.summary: The Indian rupee settled flat after briefly touching a seven-month high on Wednesday. Strong foreign portfolio investments provided support to the domestic currency. However, a stronger US dollar index limited further gains. The dollar climbed 0.2 percent on expectations of faster US interest rate increases.
stories.impact: Unclear for Nifty: A stable currency helps import costs, but dollar strength limits gains for broader emerging market assets.

stories.headline: SpiceJet board approves plan to raise up to ₹5,500 crore amid cash crunch
stories.summary: SpiceJet's board cleared a plan to raise up to 5,500 crore rupees through shares and other securities. The airline faces unpaid dues, delayed salaries and flight disruptions. The carrier plans to rebuild its fleet and improve flight reliability. Its shares hit the five percent upper limit for six straight days.
stories.impact: Little effect on Nifty: While helpful for the airline, SpiceJet is not part of the main benchmark index.

stories.headline: Gold imports may fall to $40 bn in FY27 on duty hike: Commerce Secy
stories.summary: India's gold imports may decline to 40 billion dollars in the current financial year. This is down from roughly 72 billion dollars in the prior fiscal period. Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal said import duty increases implemented in May have slowed shipments. Lower gold purchases help narrow India's trade deficit.
stories.impact: May help Nifty: Lower trade deficits support the rupee, which can reduce imported inflation risks for the broader economy.

stories.headline: RBI to conduct Overnight Variable Rate Reverse Repo (VRRR) auction under LAF on November 19, 2026
stories.summary: The Reserve Bank of India announced an auction to absorb excess cash from banks. The central bank set a 50,000 crore rupee limit for an overnight reverse repo window on November 19. The move follows an assessment of current money supply conditions in the banking system.
stories.impact: Little effect on Nifty: Daily central bank operations manage temporary bank cash levels without major long-term stock market shifts.

stories.headline: Dalmia Bharat to consider share buyback at Nov 23 board meeting
stories.summary: Dalmia Bharat announced its board will meet on November 23 to evaluate a share buyback plan. The company is India's fourth-largest cement manufacturer. Details on buyback price and size will be considered at the meeting. The firm also aims to expand production capacity to 75 million tonnes by FY28.
stories.impact: Little effect on Nifty: Dalmia Bharat's buyback will affect its own shares but has negligible impact on the Nifty index.

stories.headline: Gold drops to 14-month low as dollar, yields rise on hawkish Fed rhetoric
stories.summary: Gold prices fell to a 14-month low due to higher US bond yields and a rising US dollar. Statements from US Federal Reserve officials pointing to more rate hikes pushed precious metals down. Gold dropped over 3 percent during the decline.
stories.impact: May hurt Nifty: Falling gold prices can hurt gold-loan companies as underlying loan collateral values decrease.
